clue.text: Cricketers attempt to get a rise

definitions.note: plural: those who take their turn at the crease with the willow

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to have a stab at something is to attempt it

explanation.surface: Cricket players trying to provoke a reaction from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the side in at the crease is said to be batting, and the players doing so are the ones who bat.

clue.text: Soft soap and dairy product increased in price

parts.note: butter is a product of the dairy
prices that have gone up have increased

explanation.surface: A shopper grumbling that soap and butter have both gone up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' is not a cleaning product but the verb for flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for flattering someone in order to win them over.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like waterside plant

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying up a hill to watch wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb of haste; it is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags and hinds are woodland creatures, so the plural noun names some animals.

clue.text: No one doubts what this signal means

definitions.text: No one doubts what this signal means

parts.words: No one doubts what this signal means
parts.note: the signal is the one that tells people danger is over, and its message is plain to everybody: there is nothing obscure in it

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain signal is perfectly unambiguous.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the signal's name itself describes its meaning being unmistakable.
explanation.definitionFit: The siren after an air raid announced safety, and its name also says the meaning is perfectly plain.

definitions.meaning: the ground-floor seating in a British theatre, below the circle
also stops dead, as an engine does

explanation.surface: A choice between sitting and standing at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground-floor seats of a theatre carry this name, and so do market booths or stands.

parts.note: not an electoral system but a small replica built exactly to proportion

explanation.surface: A modest instance of a voting system that allocates seats by share of the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proportional representation' is the voting system; here it means a likeness made in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature replica reproduces something faithfully in reduced proportions, so it literally represents proportionally.

clue.text: It should grow by more development

indicators.note: development reshapes the letters of the two words before it into a new form

explanation.surface: Something expected to get bigger through further development.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn creature in its earliest stage is expected to grow into a full organism.

indicators.note: involved, meaning tangled or twisted, says the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A handful of people caught up in public disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a small group, especially of musicians.

parts.note: cute means charmingly or quaintly attractive

explanation.surface: A charming French way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' looks like a way of speaking; it is the mark over an e, as in café.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising diacritic over é in French is named this kind of accent mark.

parts.note: read as 'he does arrive in the end' it hides the sense 'he arrives after everyone else'

explanation.surface: Relief that an expected guest has arrived in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after all' seems to mean 'in the end'; read literally it means later than everybody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives behind everyone else is a tardy arrival.

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the word's letters might be the answer

explanation.surface: A comedian whose mocking material might cross the line into bigotry.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses wit and ridicule to criticise, so the adjective means mocking with humour.

clue.text: Old ship under last bit of sail makes slow movement

indicators.note: in an across clue, under places the ship after the letter, as if lower in a column
the final letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel with little canvas left making slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is a section of a musical work, not physical motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece or section played very slowly and broadly takes its name from the tempo marking.

parts.note: 'cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'blimey!'

indicators.note: capsized, overturned, says the letters of the name are turned about

explanation.surface: An exclamation as Alec overturns the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker-and-hide craft used in Wales and Ireland is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Game to take the helm, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to cox a rowing boat is to steer it

explanation.surface: Willingness to take charge of steering, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the adjective 'willing'; it is game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Male game birds such as pheasant are shot as game.

definitions.meaning: a strongly held opinion or certainty
a court's finding that someone is guilty of an offence

explanation.surface: Being certain about a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strongly held opinion and a formal finding of guilt in court.

clue.text: Problem with World War I battle citation

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Mons in Belgium was the first British battle of the First World War, in 1914

explanation.surface: A historian's difficulty with a reference to a Great War battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'citation' is not a footnote reference but an order to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation in law is an official order calling someone to appear before a court.

clue.text: Prevent a total loss and rescue about 50

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to rescue is to save
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A salvage effort to stop everything being lost, saving around fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old verb it means to salvage, saving goods from being wholly lost.

clue.text: Bird you shouldn't be seen with indoors?

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table

definitions.text: you shouldn't be seen with indoors?
definitions.meaning: etiquette says a man should remove his hat on entering a building, so wearing headgear indoors is frowned on

explanation.surface: A bird you would be embarrassed to be seen with inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second sense: headwear still worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A fattened castrated cockerel is a table bird, and split in two the word describes headwear still worn.

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation of requiescat in pace, 'rest in peace', carved on tombs
a tear rhyming with 'fair', a split in fabric

explanation.surface: A tombstone's words bringing a tear to a mourner's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' reads as weeping; it is a rent in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin initials for rest in peace are carved on tombs, and the same word means a rent in cloth.

clue.text: Put the case against the euro

definitions.meaning: to put forward an argument or proposition for consideration
split in two: in favour of the British currency rather than the single European one

explanation.surface: Arguing the case against the European single currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a theory for consideration is to put the case, and split it reads as favouring sterling.

parts.note: not a long-winded oration but speaking slowly, stretching out the vowels

explanation.surface: An instruction to deliver a long-winded oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protracted speech' seems to mean a lengthy address; it is drawn-out pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak lazily with long-drawn vowels is to stretch out one's words.

clue.text: Get bill reduced, strange to tell

parts.note: a/c, short for account, is a bill written in reduced form
quaint means oddly old-fashioned or strange

explanation.surface: Getting a bill knocked down, odd as it is to relate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange to tell' looks like a phrase meaning 'oddly enough'; 'tell' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone aware of something is to inform or tell them of it.

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters enclose the numeral
agitated, stirred up, means the letters of the next word are shaken about

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Flustered women of around fifty dashing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places L inside SALIED, the anagram of LADIES from 'Agitated'.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge out suddenly, as troops do from a besieged position, is to make a sortie.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable person of fifty-one who is held accountable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being legally answerable for something, as for a debt, means being responsible for it.

clue.text: Be up in time for a serious discussion

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other piece

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the short word over so it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: Being awake in good time for a weighty conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be up' looks like 'be awake'; in a down clue 'up' turns the little word over before it goes into the appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument between opposing sides is a serious discussion.

explanation.surface: Someone tending towards underhand behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' looks like 'tending to'; it means slanting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slanting at an angle and roundabout or indirect in manner.

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A coy question about a secret affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' is slang for a lover; split it, with 'on the side' meaning aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Set to one side or separate from others, as in 'kept aside', is a sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Bring in a number to help — sharpish!

indicators.note: bring in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: aid means help
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

explanation.surface: An urgent call to bring someone in quickly to assist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharpish' reads as 'quickly'; it means sour-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour or tart in taste, sharp on the tongue.

clue.text: Unusually bad actors heard on the radio

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Poor performers who are only heard, on radio drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transmitted over the airwaves is sent out to listeners, as a radio programme is.

parts.note: to obscure a light is to dim it

explanation.surface: A rare oriental coin of uncertain origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The American ten-cent piece is a coin.

definitions.meaning: a flower in crosswords is something that flows: the river in north-east England
small pegs on which a golf ball is placed for driving

explanation.surface: A flower and some pegs, as in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river (it flows), here the one in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The river through Middlesbrough is a flower in the crossword sense, and golf ball supports are pegs.

clue.text: Unusually long title to describe The Wages of Sin?

definitions.text: to describe The Wages of Sin?
definitions.note: an adjective phrase: the answer is a word that would describe such wages

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the next two words are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A book's oddly long title, describing a novel called The Wages of Sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Wages of Sin' looks like a book title; it is money earned by wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Money earned through wrongdoing is acquired dishonestly, the very sense of the adjective.

clue.text: It's the minister's place to designate names

indicators.note: designate, read as de-sign, says the letters of the word are taken out of their order and remade

explanation.surface: A minister's duty to choose the names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a government post; here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Presbyterian minister's official house is the place where the clergyman lives.
